summaryHeading: Socorro police wrote the ticket? Here is where the case actually is
summary: Socorro Municipal Court is the City of Socorro's court. The Texas Office of Court Administration lists it at 860 N. Rio Vista Rd., Socorro, TX 79927, phone (915) 872-8574. City Hall is separate, at 124 S. Horizon Blvd.
If the agency on your citation is the Socorro Police Department, the case is here. Sheriff, DPS and constable tickets on the same roads go to the El Paso County JP precinct noted on the ticket.
Paying the ticket enters a plea and results in a conviction on your driving record. Fines and court costs are set by the court.
Our flat fee for Socorro Municipal Court is $69 per citation, with discounted add-ons for extra tickets from the same stop. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: How to Tell Your Ticket Is in Socorro Municipal Court
paragraphs: Socorro sits between El Paso and San Elizario, and North Loop Dr, Alameda Ave (Highway 20) and Socorro Rd all pass through it. Drivers from El Paso, Horizon City, Clint and San Elizario cross the city every day on the way to work, so a Socorro ticket is common for people who have never lived there. The agency line on the citation is what matters: if it says Socorro Police Department, the case is filed in Socorro Municipal Court.

Three other agencies work the same roads and file elsewhere. A Sheriff's deputy, a DPS trooper or a constable files in the Justice of the Peace precinct written on the ticket; El Paso County's JP Precinct 5 office is at 9521 Socorro Rd. in the Lower Valley. An El Paso police officer on the city side of the line files at El Paso Municipal Court. If you cannot read the agency line, our free ticket and warrant lookup can confirm the court.

sections.heading: Where Socorro Municipal Court Is
paragraphs: The Texas Office of Court Administration's statewide directory lists Socorro Municipal Court at 860 N. Rio Vista Rd., Socorro, TX 79927, phone (915) 872-8574, with a presiding municipal judge. That is a different building from Socorro City Hall, which El Paso County lists at 124 S. Horizon Blvd. The city's website is ci.socorro.tx.us. We were not able to confirm the court's public hours or docket days from the city's own pages, so call the court before visiting, or let our office handle the appearance.

Whatever the hours, the rule is the same as in every Texas Class C court: paying the ticket is a plea of guilty or no contest, the court reports the conviction to DPS, and it sits on the driving record your insurer sees. If you plan to contest the ticket, do not pay it and do not request defensive driving at the window, because that request is also a plea.

sections.heading: The Socorro Tickets We See Most, and How Each Is Handled
paragraphs: The mix of Socorro tickets at our office is heavy on speeding, often on North Loop where the posted limit drops through neighborhoods, and on paperwork charges: failure to maintain financial responsibility, expired registration, no driver's license and driving while license invalid. Stops that produce two or three citations at once are common, and we handle each additional ticket at a discounted add-on rate rather than a second full fee.

Paperwork charges are where the first move is obvious. If you had a valid policy on the date of the stop, or you have since renewed the registration or obtained a license, we present that proof to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal on compliance. That is why the first thing we ask new Socorro clients for is a current insurance card and registration. Moving violations go through the ordinary sequence: we read the citation for defects, ask for an outright dismissal where there is a basis, and otherwise request deferred disposition, a driving safety course dismissal where you qualify, or a non-moving reduction. Each of those is in the court's discretion.

Drivers cited 25 mph or more over the limit, CDL holders and drivers with recent convictions should expect a course dismissal to be unavailable or refused; for them we go straight to a deferral or reduction argument. Tell us at intake if any of those apply.

sections.heading: What $69 Covers in Socorro Municipal Court
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in Socorro Municipal Court. That covers the appearance, every docket setting and the closing paperwork. Court fees for a deferral or course are set by the court and paid to the court. Additional citations from the same stop, speeding plus no insurance for example, are $10 to $30 add-ons at checkout. Socorro warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one and are handled with the ticket.

A paid ticket is a conviction, and a traffic conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on the driver's history, carrier and other rating factors. A no-insurance conviction can matter more than a speeding conviction with some carriers. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances. The consultation is free, and se habla español; many of our Socorro clients prefer to handle their case in Spanish.

sections.heading: Forgotten Socorro Tickets, Warrants and License Holds
paragraphs: Because so many Socorro tickets go to drivers who do not live there, forgotten citations are common. A missed appearance date can produce a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge, and in general an unresolved case can be reported to the state's Failure to Appear program, which blocks a DPS license renewal until the court clears the hold. Many clients first learn about an old Socorro ticket when DPS refuses to renew their license.

We file the appearance, request the warrant recall and ask the court to reset the ticket on its next docket, as described on the traffic warrant recall and OMNI hold removal pages. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.

faqs.a: The Texas Office of Court Administration lists it at 860 N. Rio Vista Rd., Socorro, TX 79927, phone (915) 872-8574. Socorro City Hall is a separate building at 124 S. Horizon Blvd. Confirm hours with the court before you go, or let us appear for you.

faqs.q: Which tickets go to Socorro Municipal Court?
faqs.a: Citations written by the Socorro Police Department inside the city, including on North Loop Dr, Alameda Ave and Socorro Rd. Sheriff, DPS and constable tickets in the same area go to the El Paso County JP precinct written on the ticket.

faqs.q: How much does a lawyer cost for a Socorro ticket?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation. Extra citations from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons, and warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one. Court fees are set by the court and paid separately.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to Socorro Municipal Court myself?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file the appearance and attend the docket for you. A personal appearance is needed only if the case is set for trial, which we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: Socorro gave me a no-insurance ticket but I was insured. Can it be dismissed?
faqs.a: If a valid policy was in force on the date of the stop, we present the proof to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal. Courts also commonly consider a compliance dismissal when coverage was obtained afterward, though that is in the court's discretion. See our no insurance ticket page.

faqs.q: Will Socorro Municipal Court give me deferred disposition?
faqs.a: Deferred disposition is available to a municipal court under Texas law, but it is granted in the judge's discretion and on the court's terms. High-speed, CDL and repeat cases are the ones most likely to be refused, which is where an attorney's request, with a dismissal argument still available, tends to matter.
